runtime.engine: native Soufflé 2.5 subprocess, no fallback evaluator
runtime.edb: in-memory managed EDB; each agent has a runtime and shares world-derived ETA/event facts; no external state mirror
runtime.persistence: No fact checkpoint file; application World remains the business-state authority.

modifiedSourceFiles.change: Optional policy_port dispatch at the existing _call tool boundary; original tool body remains the callback.
Accepts and distributes an optional adapter; one runtime per agent shares adapter facts.
Carries Concierge-to-specialist turn provenance around the existing delivery; original hub guard remains.
Constructs the adapter for scenario and interactive agent runs.
Constructs the adapter for web agents, mediates page-button tool calls with app provenance, and routes stop/arrival/expiry end notices through the same send_message gate.
Observes World state and original results; normalizes EDB facts; owns native Policy runtimes and trajectories.
Native Datalog permissions, capability, lifecycle, information-flow and isolation decisions.
Deterministic original-callback tests and trajectory export.
Exports the adapter and tool-owner map.

entrypoints.source: Concierge user turn defaults to concierge; Bus sets specialist turns to concierge.

entrypoints.authorization: ask_* tool gate plus recipient specialist tool gates

entrypoints.source: agent names and Bus turn context

entrypoints.boundary: app share sheet, stop button, planner, upload extractor and automatic updates
entrypoints.authorization: same tool gate with app provenance

entrypoints.boundary: stop, arrival and expiry end message

mechanisms: static ToolPermission declarations
Request/Parameter turn provenance
original Bus hub rejects specialist-to-specialist delivery
gaps: Agent names are reported dispatch identities, not authenticated identities.
The Concierge chat reply is model output and is not an external effect; reply guards remain original application guards.

mechanisms: Share tool ownership in Datalog
share tools require a Concierge or app turn
the app share-sheet/stop entry uses app provenance
gaps: Turn provenance is host-asserted; Python code that constructs an adapter can label a turn.
No authenticated agent identity is available.

mechanisms: RecipientTrusted produced from data/mock/contacts.json
untrusted or unknown recipients are denied for create/update/send
gaps: No structured one-off unfamiliar-recipient consent producer exists. The application therefore denies all such sends rather than inventing approval evidence.

mechanisms: one active agent-created share per recipient
recipient, field, precision, duration and place-name choices are normalized into policy inputs
gaps: The app has no persisted confirmation record binding exact recipient+fields+duration to one share. An active-share proxy is used and the original P4 guard is retained.

mechanisms: enabled fields, place-name choice, planned line mentions, coordinates and active-recipient fields are Datalog inputs
original _p5 guard remains delegated enforcement
gaps: Text classification is lexical; paraphrases that do not contain the planned line or saved-place token can escape detection.

mechanisms: duration > 240 is denied
missing duration with stop_on_arrival=false is denied
great-circle metres to the nearest sensitive saved place
precision digits exact=5, street=3, neighborhood=2
app share-sheet hide/exact choice is bound to that app share
gaps: Agent-side chat consent for an exact location has no structured producer, so exact sensitive location is denied. Invalid/missing precision normalizes conservatively to exact.

mechanisms: saved places outside the latest planned trip are denied in outbound share/message text
schedule material is separately blocked
gaps: A lexical mention test does not establish that every other-trip time or semantic trip detail is absent.

mechanisms: exact uploaded prose and texts naming at least two schedule courses are denied outbound and to Transit, Route+ETA and Share
gaps: A model may paraphrase schedule data without the original upload substring or two course tokens.

mechanisms: the original route tool only returns walking and public-transit plans
gaps: No Datalog predicate tests a requested travel mode; model prose that suggests driving is not mediated.

mechanisms: the original web UI retains its class review and confirmation controls
gaps: No policy input records reviewed schedule fields, per-field corrections or confirmation status; no confirmation lifecycle is fabricated.

mechanisms: original tools return explicit errors for unknown buildings/places; prompts forbid guessing
gaps: No Datalog relation carries null, unreadable or ambiguous extracted fields to gate planning.

mechanisms: confirmed compute_eta output is shared across agent runtimes
ETA must equal current compute_eta for RiderTrip
event sequence detects changes to delays, alerts or boarding
agent messages with time values outside the rider trip are denied
the app share sheet retains the original P2/P5-P9 path and its plan-derived arrival values
gaps: Concierge and Route+ETA prose checks remain original reply guards, not Datalog. Non-ETA route-time prose is only checked by those guards; app-originated shares are not P13-gated by the original application contract.

mechanisms: original routing excludes closed stops and departures after the last trip
original P14 checks and prompts remain
gaps: No Datalog rules encode all route feasibility constraints; doing so would duplicate the planner.

mechanisms: original Concierge P15 reply guard remains
gaps: No Datalog predicate consumes the complete route list and model reply, so P15 is delegated to the original guard.

mechanisms: update on non-active share is denied
updates less than two minutes after the previous update are denied
a changed-information flag is produced from an event-sequence advance or a newly observed ETA
gaps: Changed-information detection is event/ETA based; prose-only semantic changes remain the application call site's responsibility.

mechanisms: messages after a recipient's share ended are denied
a host-marked one-shot end notice is allowed only for the matching ended share and is recorded in ShareEndNotice
stop, arrival and expiry end notices are mediated through send_message
original arrival/expiry/revoke lifecycle is preserved
gaps: Revocation timing remains the original application lifecycle; no separate Datalog lifecycle transition is added.

mechanisms: exact alert, contact-reply and upload prose is untrusted
forwarding to specialists/shares/messages is denied
ask_user may quote it
gaps: Contact notes and semantic instructions not matching a stored untrusted string are not detected.

mechanisms: contact keys/names/channels/emails and share ids are detected in requests to Schedule, Transit and Route+ETA and denied
gaps: The detector is lexical and may miss transformed or partial contact data.

mechanisms: saved-place mentions and schedule material are denied to the Share agent
gaps: No complete request-shape validator proves that every Share-bound request contains only approved fields.

mechanisms: only Schedule owns extraction tools
other_text is removed from the confirmed extraction result before it is returned
gaps: The Schedule model can still summarize upload prose in model output; only the structured tool result is mediated.

Runtime configuration trust flag.
Stored share state; channel blank means agent-created.
Shares with no app channel (agent-created).

Planned origin/destination/stop names found in outbound text.
HH:MM tokens in outbound text.
Coordinate-shaped outbound text.
At least two schedule-course mentions or an exact stored upload/other_text substring.
Contact key/name/channel/email or share id found in a specialist request.
Any saved place name in outbound text.

Exact alert, contact-reply or upload prose substring in outbound text.
Current boarded trip, else selected trip.
Only successful original compute_eta results; shared across agent runtimes.
Monotonic freshness counter over delays, alerts and active-trip identity.

frameworkRecordingAdditions.conflictsWithExclusiveToolAllowlist: None. No framework recording tool was exposed to an agent.
frameworkRecordingAdditions.privateCapture: Policy(trace=True) records gate inputs/outcomes; test_port.py exports actual trajectories. This is operator evidence, not an agent tool.

bypasses: Model prose is not fully mediated: Concierge/Route+ETA reply guards and P15 are original application guards, not Datalog decisions.
The web schedule review/confirm state is application UI state, not a policy input; P11 has no Datalog coverage.
Direct edits to Python source, monkeypatching, or bypassing Agent._call/Session._tool can avoid the adapter.
Agent and app identities are reported labels; no authenticated principal provider exists.
gaps: P3: no structured consent lifecycle for unfamiliar recipients; untrusted recipients are denied.
P4: no operation-content-bound confirmation record; active-share proxy plus original guard.
P7: no structured agent-chat exact-location exception; app share-sheet exception is available.
P10/P11/P12/P14/P15: no complete Datalog model; original routing/tools/prompts/reply guards remain.
P16: changed-information detection is event/ETA based rather than a semantic diff of message contents.
P17: the original application still owns arrival, expiry and stop timing, and those transitions are observations rather than a Datalog lifecycle.
P18/P19/P20: text/contact classifiers are lexical and cannot prove absence of transformed data.
P21: structured extraction result is redacted; model summaries can still contain schedule prose.

tests.command: PATH=/opt/souffle/usr/bin:$PATH PYTHONPATH=/framework:$PWD python3 -m unittest discover -s policy_port -p test_port.py -t . -v
tests.externalModelUse: None in tests. One explicitly labeled offline JSON chat fixture exercises P21.

limitations: Development tests only; they do not establish held-out semantic equivalence or complete mediation.
No authenticated principals, real contact channel or human review lifecycle are available.
Original pytest suite was not run because pytest is not installed and package installation is prohibited.
The native call count is the 24 gate events captured in the trajectory bundle; this is not a complete application call census.
Trajectory capture proves observed test gates, not complete application coverage.
